speaker: Kimi K3
text: Shriram Finance's 26.8% five-year CAGR is impressive, but that 1.78 beta means it swings nearly twice as hard as the Nifty — fine for a 10x hunt if you can stomach the -37% five-year drawdown. On the IPO question: $10 won't meet any US IPO minimum, and in India the mainboard lot size for a Reliance-calibre issue runs ~₹14-15k, so your ₹10k can't apply; SME IPOs sometimes have smaller lots but liquidity is thin. Buying Reliance on Zerodha delivery: zero brokerage, but the round-trip still costs ~₹38 (STT, exchange, SEBI, stamp, GST, DP charge) plus 20% short-term tax if you sell within a year. For auto and battery plays, Tata Motors (₹700-800) and Exide (₹300-400) fit your ₹10k budget as whole shares; in the US you can buy fractional slices of Tesla, Rivian or QuantumScape with your $100.
